PERF-PY-15.name: ORM Composite Filter Without Supporting Index
PERF-PY-15.original_description: Detect recurring multi-column ORM filters without a visible supporting composite index.
PERF-PY-15.description: A hot ORM read filters on a tenant or owner key together with a time-range column, but the model declaration has no visible composite index. The database may scan and sort a large table for every request; add the index through the model or migration after validating the query plan.
PERF-PY-15.detection_notes: Match Django QuerySet filters combining an identity column and timestamp/range column when the parsed model declaration has no Index/db_index/Meta.indexes covering those columns. Unparseable index markers and external-migration comments suppress (FN-safe). SQLAlchemy shapes are not yet implemented.

PERF-PY-16.name: Retention Timestamp Predicate Without Index
PERF-PY-16.original_description: Detect time-based cleanup or purge predicates on unindexed timestamp fields.
PERF-PY-16.description: A TTL, retention, or purge path filters by a timestamp such as created_at, received_at, attempted_at, or expires_at without a visible index. Each maintenance run can scan the entire table and compete with foreground work; index the predicate or use partition lifecycle operations at larger scale.
PERF-PY-16.detection_notes: Match Django delete/filter queries comparing a DateTime field to cutoff/retention values in cleanup/purge/expire functions when no covering db_index/Index/Meta.indexes is visible for that column. Unparseable __table_args__/partition markers and external-migration comments suppress. SQLAlchemy shapes are not yet implemented.

PERF-PY-17.name: Database Connection Reuse Or Timeout Controls Missing
PERF-PY-17.original_description: Detect database engine configurations without connection recycling, pooling, or statement timeouts.
PERF-PY-17.description: A production database path does not bound connection lifetime or query duration. A runaway request can pin pooled connections and stale connections can fail under load; configure framework-appropriate recycling, health checks, pool limits, and statement timeouts.
PERF-PY-17.detection_notes: Match SQLAlchemy create_engine/create_async_engine lacking pool_recycle, pool_pre_ping, pool_timeout, or a driver statement_timeout; match Django DATABASES without CONN_MAX_AGE/CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS; match Flask SQLALCHEMY_ENGINE_OPTIONS without pool controls. Suppress tests, local SQLite settings, and controls imported from an external settings module.

PERF-PY-18.name: Repeated Regex Rewrites On The Same Input
PERF-PY-18.original_description: Detect multiple sequential regular-expression substitutions on one hot-path value.
PERF-PY-18.description: The same per-item input passes through two or more sequential regex substitutions. On a batch hot path this repeats scanning and callback overhead; combine compatible transformations or use one compiled pass when output semantics remain identical.
PERF-PY-18.detection_notes: Match a variable assigned from a value and passed through two or more re.sub or compiled-pattern.sub calls in sequence in one function. Suppress intentionally staged transforms whose patterns overlap, transformations outside request/batch code, and a helper that already combines the passes.

PERF-PY-19.name: Unbounded ORM Locking Sweep
PERF-PY-19.original_description: Detect a select-for-update expiry sweep that holds one transaction for all matching rows.
PERF-PY-19.description: A Django or SQLAlchemy maintenance job locks and processes an unbounded set of expired rows in one transaction. Lock duration and transaction memory grow with backlog and can starve foreground writes; process bounded batches with a commit between batches.
PERF-PY-19.detection_notes: Match transaction.atomic or an explicit transaction containing select_for_update/with_for_update followed by iteration without a slice, limit, keyset loop, batch helper, or per-batch commit. Suppress a statically bounded query and code whose transaction wrapper is intentionally supplied by a caller.

PERF-PY-20.name: ORM Sort Without Supporting Composite Index
PERF-PY-20.original_description: Detect an ORM equality filter followed by ordering on another column without a visible composite index.
PERF-PY-20.description: A multi-warehouse or tenant-scoped ORM query filters by one key and orders by a second column, but the model has no matching composite index. The database must sort the candidate set for every request; add the index after confirming the query plan.
PERF-PY-20.detection_notes: Match Django filter(...).order_by(...) when the parsed model lacks an index covering the equality and ordering columns as a composite prefix. Suppress external migration indexes, unparseable index markers, and queries already constrained to one primary-key row (pk=/id=). SQLAlchemy shapes are not yet implemented.

PERF-PY-21.name: Unbounded Bulk Delete In Maintenance Path
PERF-PY-21.original_description: Detect broad ORM deletes of retention or status sets without bounded batches.
PERF-PY-21.description: A maintenance command deletes a potentially large retention or status set in one ORM operation and one transaction. This can hold locks, create a large write-ahead log, and block foreground work; delete by bounded primary-key batches with intermediate commits.
PERF-PY-21.detection_notes: Match Django QuerySet.delete or SQLAlchemy Query.delete in purge, cleanup, retention, or CLI functions when no limit, key-range predicate, chunk loop, or per-batch commit is visible. Suppress explicit one-row deletes, partition drops, and maintenance paths that document a bounded table size.

PERF-PY-22.name: SQLite Backend For Concurrent Service Writes
PERF-PY-22.original_description: Detect a production-like Django or Flask configuration that falls back to SQLite while workers perform concurrent writes.
PERF-PY-22.description: A web or worker service defaults to SQLite despite a concurrent reservation or delivery path. SQLite serializes writers and can turn normal contention into database-locked failures; use the intended server database for concurrent service execution and keep SQLite scoped to tests or local-only tools.
PERF-PY-22.detection_notes: Match Django DATABASES default ENGINE sqlite3 or Flask SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI with a sqlite fallback in settings/config that also contains worker, queue, thread, or process execution. Suppress tests, fixtures, explicitly local-only development configs, and deployments that override the setting before startup.
